title: Chordal, split, threshold and cograph structure
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical structure theorems for finite simple graphs. Chordal graphs: every minimal a–b separator is a clique, a nonempty finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex, and a connected non-complete one has two non-adjacent simplicial vertices (Dirac 1961); a finite graph is chordal iff it has a perfect elimination order (Fulkerson–Gross 1965), iff it is the intersection graph of subtrees of a finite tree (Gavril 1974); a nonempty finite chordal graph has treewidth ω − 1, and every finite graph has ω ≤ tw + 1. Split graphs: split iff the graph and its complement are chordal, iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or C₅ (Földes–Hammer 1977). Threshold graphs: threshold iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or P₄ (Chvátal–Hammer 1977), iff split and a cograph (no induced P₄). Mathlib has none of these graph classes; their definitions are stated in the Challenge.
